notes: Four readings recur across this family. (1) 'Profitable' and 'earnings' default to GAAP net income attributable to the parent; any operating, EBITDA or adjusted reading must be named. Adjusted figures are never XBRL facts in the financial statements (Item 10(e)(1)(ii)(C)); they sit in furnished 8-K Item 2.02 exhibits or MD&A text. (2) Period arithmetic: 10-Q income statements carry both three-month and year-to-date contexts, cash-flow statements (the usual D&A source) are year-to-date only, there is no Q4 10-Q (Q4 = FY minus 9M for flows; never for EPS), and quarterly data is no longer routinely required in the 10-K since the 2021 Item 302 amendments. A 2026 SEC proposal (Form 10-S, semiannual reporting) is not adopted as of this run; if adopted, TTM-from-quarters will fail for opting companies and must fall back to half-years. (3) Element vintages: SalesRevenueNet, SalesRevenueGoodsNet, SalesRevenueServicesNet, CostOfGoodsSold and CostOfServices were deprecated in the 2018-01-31 taxonomy and are gone from 2021+ schemas; RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax first appears in 2017; EarningsPerShareBasicAndDiluted was deprecated in 2022 and is gone from 2025+; InterestExpenseNonoperating/Operating and the ASU 2023-07 segment-expense elements appear from 2024. Series must be stitched by period, not by element. (4) Every 'high/low' judgement here is comparative (own history or industry); the only absolute lines are sign tests (profit vs loss, growth vs decline), the SEC's two-year recurrence rule for 'non-recurring', the S&P index-eligibility test, Piotroski's ROA>0 signal, ROIC/ROE versus the cost of capital (which needs market data), and practitioner rules of thumb explicitly labelled as such. Ratios computed only from GAAP inputs (margins, ROE, ROA, turnover) are not non-GAAP measures (Item 10(e)(4)); EBITDA, adjusted earnings, organic growth and company ROIC are.
